Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.

Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# thokr
✨ sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

[![GitHub Build Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml)

[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-default.svg)](./LICENSE.md)
[![Crate Version](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/thokr)](https://crates.io/crates/thokr)
[![Github Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/thatvegandev/thokr)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/stargazers)

![demo](https://github.com/thatvegandev/assets/raw/main/thokr/demo.gif)

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

```
thokr 0.4.1
sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

USAGE:
    thokr [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    -f, --full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>
            number of sentences to use in test

    -h, --help
            Print help information

    -l, --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>
            language to pull words from [default: english] [possible values: english, english1k,
            english10k]

    -p, --prompt <PROMPT>
            custom prompt to use

    -s, --number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>
            number of seconds to run test

    -V, --version
            Print version information

    -w, --number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>
            number of words to use in test [default: 15]

```


## Installation

### Cargo

```sh
$ cargo install thokr
```

### Docker

```sh
$ docker run -it thatvegandev/thokr
```

### Arch Linux

Install `thokr-git` from the AUR

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

### Examples

| command                     |                                                    test contents |
|:----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------:|
| `thokr`                     |                          50 of the 200 most common english words |
| `thokr -w 100`              |                         100 of the 200 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 100 -l english1k` |                        100 of the 1000 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 10 -s 5`          | 10 of the 200 most common English words (hard stop at 5 seconds) |
| `thokr -p "$(cat foo.txt)"` |                   custom prompt with the output of `cat foo.txt` |
| `thokr -f 4`                | 4 grammatical sentences with full stops; overrides word settings |

_During a test you can press ← to start over or → to see a new prompt (assuming
you didn't supply a custom one)_

## Supported Languages

The following languages are available by default:

| name         |                     description |
| :----------- | ------------------------------: |
| `english`    |   200 most common English words |
| `english1k`  |  1000 most common English words |
| `english10k` | 10000 most common English words |

## Logging

Upon completion of a test, a row outlining your results is appended to the
`log.csv` file found in the following platform-specific folders. This way you
can easily track your progress over time.

| platform | value                                                            |                                        example |
| :------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| Linux    | $XDG*CONFIG_HOME/\_project_path* or $HOME/.config/_project_path_ |                      /home/colby/.config/thokr |

| Windows  | {FOLDERID*RoamingAppData}\_project_path*\config                  |    C:\Users\Colby\AppData\Roaming\thokr\config |

# thokr
✨ sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

[![GitHub Build Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml)
[![GitHub Deploy Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/deploy.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/deploy.yml)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-default.svg)](./LICENSE.md)
[![Crate Version](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/thokr)](https://crates.io/crates/thokr)
[![Github Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/thatvegandev/thokr)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/stargazers)

![demo](https://github.com/thatvegandev/assets/raw/main/thokr/demo.gif)

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

```
thokr 0.4.1
sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

USAGE:
    thokr [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    -f, --full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>
            number of sentences to use in test

    -h, --help
            Print help information

    -l, --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>
            language to pull words from [default: english] [possible values: english, english1k,
            english10k]

    -p, --prompt <PROMPT>
            custom prompt to use

    -s, --number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>
            number of seconds to run test

    -V, --version
            Print version information

    -w, --number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>
            number of words to use in test [default: 15]

```


## Installation

### Cargo

```sh
$ cargo install thokr
```

### Docker

```sh
$ docker run -it thatvegandev/thokr
```

### Arch Linux

Install `thokr-git` from the AUR

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

### Examples

| command                     |                                                    test contents |
|:----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------:|
| `thokr`                     |                          50 of the 200 most common english words |
| `thokr -w 100`              |                         100 of the 200 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 100 -l english1k` |                        100 of the 1000 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 10 -s 5`          | 10 of the 200 most common English words (hard stop at 5 seconds) |
| `thokr -p "$(cat foo.txt)"` |                   custom prompt with the output of `cat foo.txt` |
| `thokr -f 4`                | 4 grammatical sentences with full stops; overrides word settings |

_During a test you can press ← to start over or → to see a new prompt (assuming
you didn't supply a custom one)_

## Supported Languages

The following languages are available by default:

| name         |                     description |
| :----------- | ------------------------------: |
| `english`    |   200 most common English words |
| `english1k`  |  1000 most common English words |
| `english10k` | 10000 most common English words |

## Logging

Upon completion of a test, a row outlining your results is appended to the
`log.csv` file found in the following platform-specific folders. This way you
can easily track your progress over time.

| platform | value                                                            |                                        example |
| :------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| Linux    | $XDG*CONFIG_HOME/\_project_path* or $HOME/.config/_project_path_ |                      /home/colby/.config/thokr |
| macOS    | $HOME/Library/Application Support/_project_path_                 | /Users/Colby/Library/Application Support/thokr |
| Windows  | {FOLDERID*RoamingAppData}\_project_path*\config                  |    C:\Users\Colby\AppData\Roaming\thokr\config |

## Roadmap

- [ ] ⚡️ Performance
  - Right now there are known performance issues surrounding the rendering of
    the tui at each tick interval and/or key press. Ideally each render uses the
    prior render as a base and only makes the necessary adjustments (possibly
    using
    [StatefulWidget](https://docs.rs/tui/0.10.0/tui/widgets/trait.StatefulWidget.html)),
    but I haven't been able to figure that out yet.
- [ ] 🔠 Multi-language support
  - I decided not to launch thokr with languages besides english because of some
    odd rendering issues I was experiencing when trying to input characters with
    accents. It's as though I'm not able to properly input the character in [raw
    mode](https://docs.rs/crossterm/0.3.0/crossterm/raw/index.html). I'd love to
    have that figure out before shipping other languages because I personally
    felt the experience was a bit jarring. I'll open an bug report for it with
    more details and replication steps -- would love more eyes on that problem!
- [ ] 🧪 Tests
  - I've only written a small amount of tests at this point. I haven't sat down
    to really think through what tests look like when the output is dependent on
    the users terminal size, font size, etc. If you have any ideas for this please
    open up an issue and start the discussion!

## Contributing

All contributions are **greatly appreciated**.

If you have a suggestion that would make thokr better, please fork the repo and
create a [pull request](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/pulls). You can
also simply open an issue and select `Feature Request`

1. Fork the repo
2. Create your feature branch (`git checkout -b [your_username]/xyz`)
3. Commit your changes (`git commit -m 'add some xyz'`)
4. Rebase off main (`git fetch --all && git rebase origin/main`)
5. Push to your branch (`git push origin [your_username]/xyz`)
6. Fill out pull request template

See the [open issues](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/issues) for a full
list of proposed features (and known issues).

import subprocess, time, os, sys, shlex

def tmux(*args):
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux"]+list(args), capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r

def capture(session, extra=[]):
    r=tmux("capture-pane","-t",session,"-p",*extra)
    return r.stdout

def kill(session):
    tmux("kill-session","-t",session)

def start(session, cmd, w=80, h=24, env=None):
    kill(session)
    env_args=[]
    if env:
        for k,v in env.items(): env_args+=["-e", f"{k}={v}"]
    # new-session
    r=tmux("new-session","-d","-s",session,"-x",str(w),"-y",str(h),*env_args, cmd)
    print("new", r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode)
    time.sleep(0.8)
    print(capture(session))
    print("--- with escapes ---")
    print(repr(capture(session, ["-e"])))

if __name__=="__main__":
    cmd=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else "/workspace/executable -p 'hello world'"
    w=int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv)>2 else 80
    h=int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv)>3 else 24
    start("probe", cmd, w, h)
    # leave running? caller kill

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"/tmp"); from helper import Tmux
import subprocess, time, re
def strip(s): return re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',s)
def probe(prompt,w=80,h=24):
    # escape single quote
    cmd=f"/workspace/executable -p '{prompt}'"
    t=Tmux(w=w,h=h,cmd=cmd)
    lines=strip(t.cap(True)).splitlines()
    out=[]
    for i,l in enumerate(lines):
        if l.strip():
            out.append((i, len(l)-len(l.lstrip(' ')), len(l.rstrip()), repr(l.strip()[:80]), len(l.strip())))
    print(f"w={w} h={h} promptlen={len(prompt)} prompt={prompt[:40]!r} -> {out}")
    t.kill(); subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"],capture_output=True); time.sleep(0.15)
    return out

# words separated
for nwords in [1,2,3,5,10,15,20,30]:
    p=' '.join(['word']*nwords)
    probe(p)
print("--- single long word ---")
for L in [10,30,60,69,70,71,80,100,140,141,200]:
    probe('a'*L)
print("--- heights ---")
for h in [10,20,24,25,30,40]:
    probe('hello world',h=h)
for h in [10,20,24,30]:
    probe(' '.join(['word']*20),h=h)
print("--- widths ---")
for w in [20,30,40,50,60,80,81]:
    probe('hello world',w=w)
    probe(' '.join(['word']*10),w=w)

def strip(s): return re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',s)

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"/tmp"); from helper import Tmux
import subprocess, time, re
def strip(s): return re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',s)
def top(prompt,w=80,h=24):

    t=Tmux(w=w,h=h,cmd=cmd)
    lines=strip(t.cap(True)).splitlines()
    rows=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.strip()]
    t.kill(); subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"],capture_output=True); time.sleep(0.12)
    return rows[0] if rows else None, len(rows)

def inferH(prompt,label):
    Hs=set(range(0,30))
    for h in [24,25,10,11,20,21]:
        y,n=top(prompt,h=h)
        s={H for H in range(30) if (h-H)//2==y}
        Hs&=s
        print(label,f"h={h} y={y} vis={n} possibleH={sorted(s)}")
    print(label,"=> H",sorted(Hs))

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"/tmp"); from run_custom import run_seq
# Helper to create typing schedule: chars in buckets: we need timestamps
# Bucket1 t=0.. <1, bucket2 1-2, bucket3 2-3, bucket4 3-4 final
# Schedule by absolute target delays between.
def schedule(prompt, times):
    # times absolute from first approx, convert to delays
    seq=[]; prev=0
    for ch,t in zip(prompt,times):
        seq.append((ch, max(0,t-prev) if False else 0)) # placeholder
    # we need delay AFTER each char = next_time - curr_time
    seq=[]
    for i,ch in enumerate(prompt):
        d=(times[i+1]-times[i]) if i+1<len(times) else 0
        seq.append((ch,d))
    return seq

# counts [1,2,3,1] prompt 7 a's: b1: t0, b2:1.1,1.2, b3:2.1,2.2,2.3, b4:3.1 -> sd excl last of [1,2,3] pop=0.816 -> expect 0.82
run_seq("aaaaaaa", schedule("aaaaaaa",[0,1.1,1.2,2.1,2.2,2.3,3.1]))

import subprocess,time,re,os,shutil
def strip(s): return re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',s)
def probe(cmd, typed="h", total=4, home="/tmp/fakehome_timer"):
    if os.path.exists(home): shutil.rmtree(home)
    os.makedirs(home)
    t=Tmux(cmd=cmd,home=home)
    print("CMD",cmd,"initial")
    for i,l in enumerate(t.cap().splitlines()):
        if l.strip(): print(i,repr(l.rstrip()))
    if typed:
        for ch in typed: subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",t.sess,"-l",ch]); time.sleep(0.05)
    start=time.time()
    last=None
    while time.time()-start<total:
        cap=strip(t.cap(True))
        lines=[l.rstrip() for l in cap.splitlines() if l.strip()]
        sig=tuple(lines)
        if sig!=last:
            print(f"t~{time.time()-start:.2f}", lines)
            last=sig
        time.sleep(0.05)
    print("log"); t.log()
    t.kill(); subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"],capture_output=True); time.sleep(0.15)

import subprocess,time,re,os,shutil
def strip(s): return re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',s)
def timed(prompt,items,secs):
    home="/tmp/fh_sd_timer"
    if os.path.exists(home): shutil.rmtree(home)
    os.makedirs(home)
    t=Tmux(cmd=f"/workspace/executable -p '{prompt}' -s {secs}",home=home)
    for i,(ch,tx) in enumerate(items):
        delay=(items[i+1][1]-tx if i+1<len(items) else 0)
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",t.sess,"-l",ch]); time.sleep(delay)
    time.sleep(secs+1)
    cap=[l.strip() for l in strip(t.cap(True)).splitlines() if l.strip()]
    print("items",items,"summary",[x for x in cap if 'acc' in x], "top/x",cap[:1])
    t.log()
    t.kill(); subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"],capture_output=True); time.sleep(0.1)

import os, subprocess, time, shutil, sys
sys.path.insert(0,"/tmp"); from helper import Tmux
# Test path env precedence: helper sets HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME both. Need custom tmux start to vary.
# We'll use tmux sessions manually with -e vars.
def run(env, label):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"],capture_output=True)
    # clean possible dirs
    sess="probe"
    args=["tmux","new-session","-d","-s",sess,"-x","80","-y","24"]
    for k,v in env.items(): args+=["-e",f"{k}={v}"]
    args.append("/workspace/executable -p 'ab'")
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True)
    time.sleep(0.6)
    for ch in "ab":
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",sess,"-l",ch]); time.sleep(0.05)
    time.sleep(0.4)
    print("\n",label,env)
    for rootbase in [env.get("HOME",""), env.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME",""), "/tmp/homeA","/tmp/xdgB","/tmp/homeNoXdg"]:
        if rootbase and os.path.exists(rootbase):
            for root,dirs,files in os.walk(rootbase):
                for f in files:
                    p=os.path.join(root,f); print(" found",p, open(p).read().strip().splitlines()[-1] if os.path.getsize(p) else "empty")

import pty, os, subprocess, time, select, sys, tty, termios, struct, fcntl, signal

def set_winsize(fd, rows=24, cols=80):
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0))

def run(args, inputs=[], wait=0.5, rows=24, cols=80, env_extra=None):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid==0:
        os.environ["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
        os.environ["HOME"]="/tmp/ptyhome"

import pty, os, subprocess, time, select, sys, termios, struct, fcntl, signal, shutil

def run(prog,args,inputs=[],wait=0.5,rows=24,cols=80):
    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/ptyhome",ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs("/tmp/ptyhome")
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid==0:
        os.environ["TERM"]="xterm-256color"; os.environ["HOME"]="/tmp/ptyhome"
        os.execv(prog,[prog]+args)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0))
    def drain(timeout):
        end=time.time()+timeout; data=b""
        while time.time()<end:
            r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.05)
            if fd in r:
                try: chunk=os.read(fd,65536)
                except OSError: break
                if not chunk: break
                data+=chunk
        return data
    outs=[drain(wait)]
    for data,delay in inputs:
        os.write(fd,data); outs.append(drain(delay))
    wpid,status=os.waitpid(pid,os.WNOHANG)
    code=os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status) if wpid else None
    if not wpid:
        os.kill(pid,signal.SIGKILL); os.waitpid(pid,0)
    os.close(fd)
    log=None
    try: log=open("/tmp/ptyhome/.config/thokr/log.csv","rb").read()
    except: pass
    return outs,code,log

def cmp(label,args,inputs):
 a=run('/tmp/refbin/executable',args,inputs); b=run('/tmp/mybin/executable',args,inputs)

  print('DIFF',label)
  for i,(x,y) in enumerate(zip(a[0],b[0])):
   if x!=y: print(' step',i,'REF',repr(x)); print('     MINE',repr(y))
  print(' codes/logs',a[1:],b[1:])

def run(prog):
 pid,fd=pty.fork()
 if pid==0:
  os.environ['TERM']='xterm';os.environ['HOME']='/tmp/ptyhome';os.execv(prog,[prog,'-p','hello world'])
 def sz(r,c):fcntl.ioctl(fd,termios.TIOCSWINSZ,struct.pack('HHHH',r,c,0,0))
 sz(24,80);time.sleep(.3)

  d=b''
  while select.select([fd],[],[],0)[0]:d+=os.read(fd,65536)
  return d

 print('resize 100x30'); sz(30,100); os.kill(pid,signal.SIGWINCH); time.sleep(.4); print(repr(drain()))
 os.kill(pid,9);os.waitpid(pid,0)

        if arg.starts_with('-') {
            s.push_str(&format!(
                "\n\tIf you tried to supply `{}` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- {}`\n",
                arg, arg
            ));
        }
        s.push_str(&format!("\nUSAGE:\n    {} [OPTIONS]", self.bin));
        s.push_str(self.footer());
        self.err(s)
    }

    fn unknown_short(&self, c: char) -> ! {
        let a = format!("-{}", c);
        self.err(format!(
            "error: Found argument '{}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\n\tIf you tried to supply `{}` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- {}`\n\nUSAGE:\n    {} [OPTIONS]{}",
            a, a, a, self.bin, self.footer()
        ))
    }

    fn unknown_long(&self, display: &str, name_for_suggestion: &str) -> ! {
        let suggestion = suggestion_for_long(name_for_suggestion);
        let mut s = format!(
            "error: Found argument '{}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n",
            display
        );
        if let Some(sug) = suggestion {
            s.push_str(&format!("\n\tDid you mean '--{}'?\n", sug.long_name()));
        }
        s.push_str(&format!(
            "\n\tIf you tried to supply `{}` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- {}`\n\n{}",
            display,
            display,
            self.usage_block(suggestion)
        ));
        s.push_str(self.footer());
        self.err(s)
    }

    fn unexpected_value_for_flag(&self, flag: &str, value_with_eq: &str) -> ! {
        // Exactly as clap renders this error: no "USAGE:" label.
        self.err(format!(
            "error: The value '{}' was provided to '{}' but it wasn't expecting any more values\n\n{}{}{}",
            value_with_eq,
            flag,
            self.bin,
            self.usage_context(None),
            self.footer()
        ))
    }

    fn missing_value(&self, opt: Opt) -> ! {
        let mut s = format!(
            "error: The argument '{}' requires a value but none was supplied\n",
            opt.canonical()
        );
        if opt == Opt::SupportedLanguage {
            s.push_str("\t[possible values: english, english1k, english10k]\n");
        }
        s.push_str(&format!("\nUSAGE:\n    {} [OPTIONS]", self.bin));
        s.push_str(self.footer());
        self.err(s)
    }

    fn multiple_occurrence(&self, opt: Opt) -> ! {
        self.err(format!(
            "error: The argument '{}' was provided more than once, but cannot be used multiple times\n\nUSAGE:\n    {} [OPTIONS]{}",
            opt.canonical(),
            self.bin,
            self.footer()
        ))
    }

    fn invalid_utf8(&self) -> ! {
        self.err(format!(
            "error: Invalid UTF-8 was detected in one or more arguments\n\nUSAGE:\n    {} [OPTIONS]{}",
            self.bin,
            self.footer()
        ))
    }

    fn invalid_numeric(&self, opt: Opt, value: &str, parse_err: &std::num::ParseIntError) -> ! {
        self.err(format!(
            "error: Invalid value \"{}\" for '{}': {}\n\nFor more information try --help\n",
            value,
            opt.canonical(),
            parse_err
        ))
    }

    fn invalid_language(&self, value: &str) -> ! {
        let sug = suggestion_for_value(value, &["english", "english1k", "english10k"]);
        let mut s = format!(
            "error: \"{}\" isn't a valid value for '{}'\n\t[possible values: english, english1k, english10k]\n",
            value,
            Opt::SupportedLanguage.canonical()
        );
        if let Some(v) = sug {
            s.push_str(&format!("\n\tDid you mean \"{}\"?\n", v));
        }
        let parts: Vec<String> = self
            .distinct_opts()
            .iter()
            .map(|o| o.canonical().to_owned())
            .collect();
        s.push_str(&format!("\nUSAGE:\n    {} {}", self.bin, parts.join(" ")));
        s.push_str(self.footer());
        self.err(s)
    }
}
